payload.title: Engagement Ring Insurance and How to Get It
payload.excerpt: Contents, standalone or travel cover? What to check in a policy, the paperwork to keep, and how to protect your ring on a proposal or wedding abroad.
key_takeaways: A contents policy can cover your ring, but per-item limits mean you may need to add it and check its value against the limit.
Travel insurance often caps each valuable item and rarely pays for theft of anything left unattended, so it is not a substitute for jewellery cover.
Keep the receipt, grading report, a valuation and photos together, and have the ring revalued about every two years.
If a claim goes wrong, complain to the insurer first and then take it to AFCA, which is free and independent.

faq.q: Is my engagement ring covered by home contents insurance?
faq.a: It can be. Contents insurance covers personal belongings, including jewellery, if they are damaged, lost or stolen, but most policies limit what you can claim for certain items. Check whether the ring needs to be added with its own value.

faq.q: Does travel insurance cover my engagement ring overseas?
faq.a: Travel insurance can cover lost, damaged or stolen valuables, but policies often limit each item's value. Theft of unattended items, items not in an available hotel safe and items in checked baggage are typically excluded.

faq.q: Does insurance cover a lost engagement ring or a lost stone?
faq.a: It depends on the policy. Check that it covers loss and damage as well as theft. Ask your insurer directly how a stone lost from its setting is treated.

faq.q: Should I insure the ring before I propose?
faq.a: Ask your insurer how and when a new ring can be added before you collect it. If you are proposing abroad, carry it on board and tell your insurer your travel dates.

faq.q: What is the difference between agreed value and market value?
faq.a: In general terms, agreed value is a fixed amount set when you take out or renew a policy, and market value is assessed at claim time and can fall. Jewellery policies vary, so check which basis yours uses.

faq.q: How often should I get my engagement ring revalued?
faq.a: The Jewellers Association of Australia recommends approximately every two years. Update the insured value at the next renewal.
